notable_absence.finding: Webhooks is the most restrictive of the three: no Advanced Template (payload structure is fixed and stated as non-modifiable - 'you cannot modify the structure of your alert payload' per webhook-reference.md), and no disable/re-enable lifecycle - 'You cannot disable a Webhooks alert integration. You can delete and re-create it when needed', unlike Slack and Microsoft Teams which both explicitly support Disable/Enable. This is a genuine capability gradient across the three integrations (Slack has the most connection/customization options, Webhooks the fewest), not just a payload-format difference.

cross_component_finding: Prerequisites (roles, Enterprise/Developer Pro Support Plan gate, 3-address firewall allowlist, up to 5 integrations per project) are verbatim-identical to configure-slack-integration.md and configure-microsoft-integration.md - the shared-shell side of the hypothesis confirmed a third time. But Webhooks diverges furthest from the other two on the lifecycle/customization axis: fixed payload (webhook-reference.md), Basic or Bearer auth only (matching configure-alert-integration.md's generic description, suggesting Webhooks is closest to the 'base' integration type the generic page describes), and no disable capability - only delete-and-recreate.
